Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.

Kidzoi is a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model built by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in a cell-type-specific manner within the kidney, addressing the limitation that no single pretrained model covers all cell types and clinical conditions. This demonstrates that fine-tuning existing models is a practical alternative to training new models de novo.

Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.

This study builds a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes linked to 'floatptosis,' a newly described form of vacuolar cell death triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. By integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data, the authors identify floatptosis-related genes associated with patient survival and explore their links to immunotherapy response. The work is largely exploratory, introducing a novel cell-death concept into LUAD prognosis research.

Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.

This study identifies cellular senescence-associated gene signatures through pan-cancer screening and builds a prognostic risk model for bladder urothelial carcinoma that integrates multi-omics and pathological data. The model stratifies patients by risk and links senescence signals to tumor microenvironment features, offering a framework for molecular risk stratification in BLCA.

PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.

PoolParty is a new Python package that streamlines the design of DNA sequence libraries used in massively parallel reporter assays, deep mutational scanning, and other multiplex assays of variant effect. It addresses the lack of purpose-built software by providing a unified, user-friendly toolkit that reduces error-prone manual steps in library construction.

Assessing the predictive potential of the Holstein bovine sperm methylome for bull fertility using machine learning.

This study tested whether DNA methylation patterns in Holstein bull sperm can predict bull fertility using machine learning models. Using existing methylation data, the authors evaluated the predictive potential of sperm methylome profiles as biomarkers for fertility in dairy cattle. The work represents an initial assessment toward developing an operational prediction tool for bull fertility based on epigenetic data.

Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.

The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) testing 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs in three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 (30 at FDR < 0.05), with 9 shared across at least two cell lines. They then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and applied the approach to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer comparison. This provides an experimental benchmark for evaluating computational regulatory variant predictions and a framework for hypothesis-generating prioritization of non-coding risk loci.

Ultra-sensitive Mapping of Cell-free DNA-derived Methylomes Reveals Brain-specific Epigenetic Alterations Implicated in Alzheimer's Disease.

The authors applied LABS, an ultra-sensitive linear amplification-based whole-genome bisulfite sequencing method, to profile methylation in serum cell-free DNA from age- and sex-matched pathologically confirmed Alzheimer's disease cases and non-AD controls from the Rush Memory and Aging Project. They demonstrate that cfDNA-derived methylomes can reveal brain-specific epigenetic alterations associated with AD, suggesting a minimally invasive route to detecting AD-related brain changes in blood.

Agent_K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery.

Agent_K is an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the full workflow from bacterial whole-genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) identification, pathway mapping, and candidate metabolite discovery. It addresses the fragmentation of existing computational tools by integrating data processing, annotation, and analysis across heterogeneous platforms with minimal manual intervention. This enables more streamlined genome-guided natural product discovery.

Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.

The authors present Torino, a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. By adapting non-negative matrix factorization to model coverage variation across samples, Torino identifies unannotated RNA processing events and links them to disease risk across tissues, individuals, and disease states in seven vertebrate species.

Streamline CNV - A Handy Nextflow Pipeline for Chromosomal Copy Number Variation Analysis.

Streamline CNV (SLCNV) is a new Nextflow-based pipeline that automates chromosomal copy number variation analysis from low-pass whole genome sequencing data. It is designed to be user-friendly for wet-lab biologists, removing the need for computational expertise while supporting a range of copy number-related analyses.

Viscous mechanical cues encode metastatic behavior through cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling and chromatin remodeling.

This preprint shows that the viscosity of a tumor's mechanical environment can mimic the effects of stiffness on cancer cells. Cells grown on soft but viscous substrates become stiffer, accumulate YAP in the nucleus, migrate better through narrow spaces, and show changes in chromatin and gene expression similar to those seen on rigid substrates. The work links viscous mechanical cues to cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling and chromatin remodeling, suggesting viscosity is an underappreciated driver of metastatic behavior.

Combining MAVEs and computational predictors improves variant classification across ancestries in hereditary cancer genes.

This paper shows that combining multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) with population-free computational variant effect predictors can reduce ancestry-related bias in classifying variants in hereditary cancer genes. Since many standard tools are trained on datasets that under-represent global populations, integrating MAVE data with unbiased predictors yields classifications that generalize better across ancestries.

Chromatin compartment shifting is recurrent and associated with epigenetic reprogramming in prostate cancer.

By integrating Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical prostate samples spanning benign hyperplasia, primary cancer, and castration-resistant cancer, the authors mapped A/B chromatin compartment organization while correcting for copy number variation and tumor purity. They found recurrent shifts in chromatin compartments that are associated with epigenetic reprogramming during prostate cancer progression. This suggests that large-scale 3D genome reorganization contributes to gene regulation changes in prostate carcinogenesis.

Catalytic DNA for Precision Diagnostics: DNAzyme-Based Approaches to Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism Detection.

This review examines DNAzyme-based biosensors for detecting single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), the most common form of human genetic variation and key biomarkers for disease risk and precision medicine. The authors argue that these catalytic DNA sensors offer advantages over conventional genotyping methods by combining programmable sequence recognition with isothermal catalytic signal amplification, enabling sensitive SNP detection even in complex biological samples.

Ultrafast alignment-free detection of viral genome variation with bronko.

The authors present bronko, an alignment-free framework that detects viral genome variants directly from sequencing reads using locality-sensitive bucketing and k-mer counting, avoiding costly read alignment. This approach enables ultrafast SNP detection that scales to massive viral sequencing datasets, addressing the computational bottleneck of traditional alignment-based variant calling pipelines.

O-acetylation mediates four distinct structural variants of the pneumococcal vaccine serotype 15A capsule polysaccharide.

This study re-examined the capsule polysaccharides of pneumococcal serogroup 15 and found that O-acetylation generates four distinct structural variants of the 15A capsule, not just the previously recognized 15A/15F pair. The work shows that conventional serological and molecular typing can miss O-acetylation-based capsule variation, which matters for vaccine coverage since 15A is included in newer conjugate vaccines.

Proteomics-Guided Discovery of Candidate Enzymes for Degradation of a Rare Pyruvylated Glycosaminogalactan by a Newly Isolated Luteolibacter Strain.

The authors isolated a new Luteolibacter strain capable of degrading EPSLp, an exopolysaccharide from Lactiplantibacillus pentosus that contains a rare pyruvylated glycosaminogalactan motif. Using proteomics to identify proteins expressed during growth on EPSLp, they discovered candidate enzymes for degrading this uncommon structure, expanding knowledge of carbohydrate-active enzyme diversity. This work provides a proteomics-guided strategy for discovering enzymes that break down poorly characterized bacterial polysaccharides.

Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.

This study uses bioinformatics analysis of public HCC transcriptomic and toxicogenomic datasets to identify HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key targets of sodium propionate, a short-chain fatty acid with epigenetic-modulating potential. In vitro experiments in hepatocellular carcinoma cells support that sodium propionate exerts anticancer activity by downregulating these histone deacetylases. The work integrates computational target prediction with cell-based validation to propose a repurposed metabolite as an epigenetic therapeutic candidate.

Conservative evolution of genetic and features in Caenorhabditis becei, an experimentally tractable gonochoristic worm.

The authors identify Caenorhabditis becei, a gonochoristic (male-female) nematode, as an experimentally tractable model for evolutionary genetics, addressing the field's over-reliance on self-fertile hermaphroditic Elegans Group species. They show that transmission-genetic properties previously characterized in androdioecious species are conserved in this Japonica Group species, making it a useful outgroup for comparative studies.

CALB1 expression in meningioma: associations with progression-free survival and chromosome arm 6q loss.

This study examined calbindin D28K (Calb), encoded by CALB1, in meningioma tissue microarrays from 147 patients, finding that CALB1 expression is associated with progression-free survival and chromosome arm 6q loss. Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges.

This review examines how large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models can be applied to predictive plant breeding, covering knowledge mining, predictive modeling, and breeding design. It serves as a critical synthesis of where these AI tools stand for crop improvement.

Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer: from carcinogenesis and molecular classification to targeted therapy.

This review synthesizes the molecular mechanisms driving colorectal cancer, from the accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations that transform normal colonic epithelium into malignancy, through molecular classification schemes, to the implications for targeted therapy. The paper serves as a consolidated reference for understanding the molecular landscape of CRC.

Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.

A recall-rescue fuzzy layer over paired Z-DNA Hunter scans for fast Z-DNA detection.

The authors present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0, a tool that improves detection of Z-DNA-forming regions by combining two scans of the existing Z-DNA Hunter at different stringency settings with a fuzzy logic layer that integrates the results. The permissive scan captures a broad candidate set while the stringent scan provides high-confidence support, aiming to balance sensitivity and specificity. This offers a fast, interpretable protocol for Z-DNA detection.

Inferring causal networks for genomic trios with high-dimensional confounding variables.

The paper introduces a new method for inferring causal relationships between molecular phenotypes (like gene expression) using genetic variants as instruments under the Mendelian randomization principle, specifically designed to handle high-dimensional confounding variables such as other genes, processes, and demographic factors. Existing methods struggle with many confounders simultaneously; this approach aims to robustly account for them when building causal networks from genomic trio data.

SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.

SCCmecExtractor is a new lightweight Python toolkit that identifies and extracts complete staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements from whole-genome assemblies by detecting degenerate attachment site patterns. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can extract the full element sequence and classify SCC elements even when they lack methicillin resistance genes. This fills a gap in mobile genetic element analysis for staphylococci.

The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.

This study tests whether metabolic traits like substrate utilization can be reliably predicted from bacterial genomes alone. Comparing four common bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria, the authors find that prediction accuracy is limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, especially for simple substrates. The results caution against assuming that genome-based metabolic predictions are universally reliable.

Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.

ogMapper improves speed and memory for short-sequencing read mapping using a novel guided sparse genome index.
